questions.q: What term does the summary use for the trap of endlessly chasing more money, status, and possessions?
questions.why: Lesson 1 explains that always wanting more keeps you on a hedonic treadmill rather than letting you enjoy the journey.

questions.q: According to the summary, reframing your job means breaking it into which three parts?
questions.why: Lesson 2 says every job is a mix of money, impact, and expression, and you must find the right ratio for you.

questions.q: What do the three letters in the ARC method stand for?
questions.why: Lesson 3 defines ARC as autonomy, relatedness, and competence, the three levers for rebuilding motivation.

questions.q: What does the summary say about finding a workplace that is completely free of stress?
a: No job is enjoyable every single moment
Only dream jobs feel truly effortless
Stress disappears once you find purpose
Remote work removes most workplace stress
questions.why: Lesson 3 says there is no job you look forward to 100 percent of the time, and accepting that is the starting point.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest you can increase your autonomy at work?
a: Overdeliver and improve your basic tasks
Ask for a new job title and more pay
questions.why: Lesson 3 recommends overdelivering and upgrading the systems you already work with to gain more freedom.
